articles.source: 2026.8.12-AI 究竟是企业的魔法，还是一场自欺欺人的表演？

paragraphs.en: I Helped Run Lululemon. Companies Need to Stop Kidding Themselves About A.I.
paragraphs.cn: 我曾参与管理Lululemon，想说在AI问题上，公司可别再自欺欺人了

paragraphs.en: Companies these days are quick to stick “A.I.” in news releases, in earnings calls, in product names, in job postings and in titles at the top of their organizations. The real question is what strategy sits behind the abbreviation. A title costs nothing, but it doesn’t produce anything, either.
paragraphs.cn: 如今许多公司热衷于在新闻稿、财报电话会议、产品名称、招聘信息，甚至高层职位名称中都加上“A.I.”这个标签。但真正的问题在于：这个缩写背后到底有何种战略作支撑？一个头衔没什么成本，但它同样也不会创造任何价值。

paragraphs.en: Talented technologists promised to crack business problems that were too complicated and expensive to solve before. This was the beginning of what I call A.I. wishing: the belief by company leaders that A.I. is magic, that you can wave its wand toward a hard problem and skip the work of solving it.
paragraphs.cn: 优秀的技术专家们曾许诺，说他们能够解决那些过去因为过于复杂、成本太高而无法解决的商业难题。这正是我所谓“AI许愿”的开始：公司领导相信 AI是一种魔法，只要对着一个棘手的问题挥挥它的魔杖，就能直接跳过解决问题所需付出的努力过程。

paragraphs.en: The demo looked like magic. But the tool wanted clean, connected data and decisions made in consistent, repeatable ways. Ours lived in a dozen systems that did not agree, layered with decades of exceptions and workarounds.
paragraphs.cn: 演示小样看着是很炫酷，但AI需要的是经过整理的、有关联的数据，还有以一致的逻辑、可重复的方式做出的决策。而我们的数据却分散在十几个彼此对不上号的系统中，还叠加了几十年来积累的各种例外案例和临时解决方案。

paragraphs.en: This brings me to A.I. washing. The insidious cousin of A.I. wishing, it is when a company — under pressure to immediately show results — claims to be doing more with A.I. than it actually is.
paragraphs.cn: 这就引出了“AI漂洗”这个概念。它是“AI许愿”的阴险近亲，指一家公司在迫于压力、需要立刻展示成果的情况下，宣称自己正在利用 AI 做很多事情，但实际上没有达到所说的程度。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the best-known version of A.I. washing is the most tragic one: the A.I. layoff. A company proclaims it needs fewer people because A.I. made its operations more efficient. Often the efficiency doesn’t exist yet. The cut is really about freeing up cash, sometimes to spend more on A.I.
paragraphs.cn: 也许最广为人知，也是最惨烈的一种AI漂洗就是“AI裁员”。公司会宣称，由于AI提高了其运营效率，因此不再需要那么多员工。很多时候，这种效率提升其实尚未实现。裁员的真正目的，是为了释放现金流，有时甚至是为了加大对AI的投入。

paragraphs.en: A.I. is a genuinely powerful technology that still needs people, and putting it to use is slow, human work. The sooner we are honest about that with our boards, our employees, our investors and the public, the sooner we can stop performing A.I. and start building something with it.
paragraphs.cn: AI确实是一项极其强大的技术，但它依然需要人的参与，能把AI真正用起来，是一个缓慢且依赖人力的过程。我们越早对董事会、员工、投资者以及公众坦诚这一点，就越能尽早停止“表演AI”，转而开始真正用它去创造一些东西。

articles.source: 2026.8.13-身心管理E01 一个晨间习惯，瞬间提升睡眠质量

paragraphs.en: I wake up in the morning and I want to reach for my phone, but I know that even if I were to crank up the brightness on that phone screen, it's not bright enough to trigger that cortisol spike and for me to be at my most alert and focused throughout the day and to optimize my sleep at night. So what I do is I get out of bed and I go outside.

And if it's a bright, clear day and the sun is low in the sky or the sun is starting to get overhead, what we call low solar angle, then I know I'm getting outside at the right time. If there's cloud cover and I can't see the sun, I also know I'm doing a good thing because it turns out, especially on cloudy days, you want to get outside and get as much light energy or photons in your eyes.

So the way to get this sunlight viewing early in the day is to look toward the sun. If it's too bright to look at directly, well, then don't do that. You just look toward it, but not directly at it. It's absolutely fine to blink. In fact, I encourage you to blink whenever you feel the impulse to blink.

I want to share with you three critical things about this tool of morning sunlight viewing. First of all, this is not some woo-woo biology thing. This is grounded in the core of our physiology. There are literally hundreds, if not thousands, of quality peer-reviewed papers showing that light viewing early in the day is the most powerful stimulus for wakefulness throughout the day, and it has a powerful positive impact on your ability to fall and stay asleep at night.

So there's this asymmetry in our retinal, our eye biology, and in our brain's biology, whereby early in the day, right around waking, you need a lot of light, a lot of photons, a lot of light energy, and artificial lights generally just won't accomplish what you need them to accomplish. But at night, even a little bit of artificial light can really mess up your so-called circadian, your 24-hour clocks and all these mechanisms that we're talking about.

items.understanding: 把…调到最大（使劲拧旋钮转到头的感觉）。crank up the brightness / volume / heat——拉高亮度/音量/暖气。近义 turn up。文中 crank up the brightness on the phone screen 提升手机屏幕亮度。
v. 触发。trigger that cortisol spike 触发皮质醇峰值；trigger a response 触发反应；trigger the release of a hormone 触发荷尔蒙分泌。A trigger B 表因果，科普高频。
v. 使达到最优。"optimize + 名词" 让某事达最佳状态：optimize sleep 让睡眠达最好 / optimize diet 让饮食达最优。
n. 光子（light energy / photons）。科普播客里常见，记一次就通。
温和建议句式"你会想要…"，区别于 you should 的外部施压感，更像善意提醒。教口语可用这区别帮学生拿捏语气。
口语）把…搞乱。mess up your sleep 搞乱睡眠；mess up your schedule 搞乱日程。书面近义 disrupt / interfere。
n.（一件事的）运作原理、机制。和 trigger / optimize 一样是科普绝对高频词。
adj.（美式口语）没事实根据、空穴来风的。This sounds sort of woo-woo, but it actually works. 听起来不切实际，但确实有效。
以…为根基/依据。be grounded in science 以科学为依据；be grounded in evidence 有实证支撑。
同行评审论文。peer 同行；review 评审。科普里常用来佐证结论可靠。

articles.source: 2026.8.13-“救命，我可能是个传统主妇”：一个职业女性的厨房自白

paragraphs.en: Help! I Might Be a Tradwife!
paragraphs.cn: 救命！我可能是个传统家庭主妇！

paragraphs.en: When I heard that Netflix was rebooting “Little House on the Prairie,” I was hopeful, if a little wary.  The “Little House” reboot arrives in the midst of a tradwife moment.
paragraphs.cn: 当得知网飞将要翻拍《草原上的小木屋》时，我心怀期待，却也略带警惕。这场《草原上的小木屋》的翻拍热潮，恰逢传统主妇风潮盛行的当下。

paragraphs.en: As a woman who’s always believed that my life purpose is synonymous not with my fecundity or my homemaking prowess but with my artistic ambitions, I’m decidedly not the audience for this kind of content.
paragraphs.cn: 我一直坚信，自己的人生价值不在于生育能力，也不在于持家本领，而在于艺术理想。因此，我显然绝不是这类内容的受众。

paragraphs.en: But maybe it was the moment when I was slicing strawberries and scooping homemade coconut-almond granola into my son’s Greek yogurt that a startling revelation dawned on me. I’m definitely not a tradwife — but maybe I’m a little tradwife-curious? Maybe I have a few latent tradwife tendencies?
paragraphs.cn: 但就在我切着草莓、把自制的椰香杏仁格兰诺拉麦片舀进儿子的希腊酸奶里的那一刻，我突然有了一个惊人的感悟。我绝对不是一个传统主妇——但我会不会对这种生活心生向往？我身上会不会潜藏着一些传统主妇的特质？

paragraphs.en: How can I renounce the regressive side of tradwives while blissfully kneading my own milk bread dough? How can I deny the appeal of the Hannah Neelemans of the world when my own household habits help balance my workaholism, keep me present and mindful in my body?
paragraphs.cn: 我该如何一边满心愉悦地揉制牛奶面包面团，一边摒弃传统主妇观念中保守落后的一面？当我的居家日常能够克制我的工作狂倾向，让我专注当下、身心沉静时，我又怎能否认汉娜·尼勒曼这类生活博主的独特吸引力呢？

paragraphs.en: So, like many others, I’m learning to reassess the value of so-called grandma hobbies, those frontier-adjacent activities that — surprise, surprise — don’t also require you to be a religious zealot or an antisuffragist.
paragraphs.cn: 所以，和很多人一样，我开始重新评估那些所谓“奶奶辈爱好”的价值。那些贴近拓荒时代的生活活动，说来意外，它们并不需要你成为宗教狂热者，也不需要你反对女性选举权。

paragraphs.en: I imagine other people find this same kind of contemplation in sewing, or knitting, or mending. So even if I don’t live the full tradwife lifestyle — for anyone else’s consumption, or my own — I can still venerate those tasks that remind me that who I am meant to be is fluid and multitudinous. It can be expressed in how I stir a wooden spoon through water and flour to make the tangzhong that is the starter for my son’s favorite milk bread, and also in a poem I might write, born of my fascination with the same word.
paragraphs.cn: 我想，其他人也能在缝纫、编织、缝补这类小事中获得同样的沉思与治愈。所以，即便我不会为了取悦他人或满足自我，完全复刻传统主妇的生活方式，我依然敬重这些琐事。它们让我明白，人的自我定位是流动且多元的。这份自我，既可以体现在我手持木勺、搅拌水和面粉，制作出儿子最爱的牛奶面包所需的烫种里，也可以体现在我提笔写下的诗句中，而这首诗正源于我对同一个词汇的着迷。

articles.source: 2026.8.14-哈佛教授的“友谊经济学”：为什么我们交不到朋友了

paragraphs.en: The Economics of Friendship
paragraphs.cn: 友谊的经济学

paragraphs.en: The ferry crossing from Chappaquiddick to Edgartown, Mass., is only 527 feet long. But no matter how rich or important you are, you have to wait to get on the boat. Someone complains about the line, the weather, politics. Someone else laughs. A conversation begins.
paragraphs.cn: 从马萨诸塞州查帕奎迪克（Chappaquiddick）到埃德加敦（Edgartown）的渡轮，航程只有527英尺。但是，无论你多有钱、多重要，你都得排队等船。有人抱怨队伍、抱怨天气、抱怨政治。然后有人笑起来。一段对话，就这样开始了。

paragraphs.en: But spending time around that ferry has made me wonder if modern life has undersold inconvenience. We treat waiting as wasted time. But sometimes waiting does something useful: It forces people into the same place long enough for conversation to begin.
paragraphs.cn: 但在渡轮那里待了一段时间后，我开始怀疑：现代生活是不是低估了"不便"的价值。我们总把等待当作浪费的时间。但有时候，等待也有它的用处：它强制人们在同一个地方待上足够长的时间，从而让一段对话得以开始。

paragraphs.en: Loneliness has become one of the stranger problems of modern life. In 2023 the U.S. surgeon general called loneliness a public-health problem.
paragraphs.cn: 孤独已成为现代生活中一个颇为奇特的问题。2023年，美国卫生总监将孤独定义为一个公共卫生问题。

paragraphs.en: Which brings me back to that ridiculously inconvenient ferry and what I call the friction theory of friendship. Some inconveniences aren't merely costs. They are the hidden scaffolding of social life. If I had to estimate my own production function for friendship, it would look something like this: friendship = (proximity × repetition) + (idle time × low stakes) + shared irritation.
paragraphs.cn: 由此我们可以说回到那艘极其不便的渡轮，以及我所谓的"友谊摩擦理论"。有些"不便"，并不只是代价。它们是社交生活隐秘的脚手架。如果要我估算自己的"友谊生产函数"，它看起来大概会是这个样子：友谊 =(距离近 × 重复遇见)+（闲暇时间×低利害情境）+共同的不满。

paragraphs.en: Proximity matters most when it recurs. Idle time matters most when nobody is trying to impress anyone. Shared irritation helps, but with diminishing returns: A delayed ferry creates conversation; a broken ferry creates rage.
paragraphs.cn: 距离近，在反复出现时最起作用。闲暇，在没人刻意表现自己的时候，最有价值。共同的不满有帮助，但效用递减：延误的渡轮，催生交谈；坏掉的渡轮，只会制造愤怒。

paragraphs.en: This is why friendship is often a product of something else: work, school, church, children, sports, errands, waiting rooms. Modern life has spent decades eliminating that friction. We can work without offices, shop without stores, exercise without gyms and communicate without looking anyone in the eye. Together they have made interaction with other people increasingly optional.
paragraphs.cn: 正因如此，友谊往往是其他事物的副产品：工作、学校、教堂、孩子、体育运动、跑腿办事、候诊室等等。然而几十年来，现代生活一直在消除这种摩擦。我们可以不用办公室工作，不用实体店购物，不用健身房锻炼，也不用与人四目相对就能交流。这些便利加在一起，让人与人之间的交往，变得越来越可有可无。

paragraphs.en: The solution isn't to make life harder for its own sake. But we should ask what social infrastructure is being lost.
paragraphs.cn: 解决之道，不是刻意把生活变难。但我们应该追问：我们正在失去什么样的社会基础设施。

paragraphs.en: Schools, for example, aren't only human-capital institutions. They are social-capital institutions. Much of what we call "community" used to be produced by institutions as a byproduct.
paragraphs.cn: 例如，学校不仅仅是人力资本机构。它还是社会资本机构。我们所说的"社区"，在很大程度上，曾经是各类机构无意之中生产的副产品。

paragraphs.en: That is why I've come to love the Chappaquiddick ferry. It gives people nothing to do for a few minutes except notice one another.
paragraphs.cn: 这就是为什么，我渐渐爱上了查帕奎迪克渡轮。在那几分钟里，人们除了互相打量之外，别无他事可做。

paragraphs.en: Convenience has saved us time. The hidden price is that it has also saved us from one another.
paragraphs.cn: 便利为我们节省了时间。但代价是，它也让我们丢失了彼此。

items.understanding: 低估…的价值（反义 oversell 高估/过度宣传）。undersold inconvenience 低估了“不便”的价值——连接右右：适度不便反而催生互动。
迫使某人进入（某种状态/地方）。forces people into the same place——强制把人凑到一处，才能起对话。
友谊摩擦理论。friction 原指摩擦/阻力，这里指“不便”反而催生友谊。可复用在我和右右的亲子互动：适度不便反而增进连接。
脚手架。the hidden scaffolding of social life——社交生活隐秘的支撑结构。比喻“看不见但撑着整体”的东西。
低利害、低压力。idle time × low stakes——闲暇 × 无压力情境，友谊更容易长出来。

articles.source: 2026.8.11-消费普遍谨慎的当下，中国人为什么愿意为运动买单？

paragraphs.en: Running, Rock Climbing and Other Sports Are Taking Off in China. Pricey Workout Clothes, Too.
paragraphs.cn: 跑步、攀岩等运动正在中国蓬勃兴起。价格不菲的运动服装也是如此。

paragraphs.en: Yangshuo in southern China has long been a rock-climbing destination for American and European tourists. But lately, a different demographic has flocked to its limestone cliffs: office workers from China’s big cities.
paragraphs.cn: 位于中国南部的阳朔长期以来一直是欧美游客的攀岩圣地。但最近，另一类人群也涌向了这里的石灰岩峭壁：来自中国各大城市的上班族。

paragraphs.en: “I needed some exercise and outdoor activities to cope with the high-pressure work environment,” Chen Xue, a 28-year-old auditor, said.
paragraphs.cn: “我需要一些运动和户外活动来应对高压的工作环境。”28岁的审计师陈雪（音译）说。

paragraphs.en: China’s rock-climbing boom is part of a larger fitness craze that has taken over the country. The number of marathon participants has doubled since 2017 to more than a million people, and Hyrox had 55,000 participants in China this past year, up from 7,300 a year earlier.
paragraphs.cn: 中国攀岩热潮不过只是席卷全国的健身热潮的一部分。自2017年以来，马拉松参赛人数已翻了一番，逾100万人；而去年，Hyrox赛事在中国吸引了5.5万名参赛者，较前一年的7300人有了大幅增长。

paragraphs.en: And alongside the fitness boom, hiking shoes and yoga pants and other types of athletic gear have become aspirational styles for China’s middle class. While foreign automakers and luxury brands are struggling against tough domestic competition in China, athletic apparel is a rare market where Western companies such as Lululemon, Hoka and Adidas are increasing sales.
paragraphs.cn: 随着这股健身热潮的兴起，徒步鞋、瑜伽裤及其他各类运动装备，已然成为中国中产阶级向往的穿搭风格。外国车企和奢侈品牌尚在中国激烈的本土竞争中苦苦挣扎，运动服饰却成了一方罕见的市场，像Lululemon、Hoka和阿迪达斯这样的西方品牌，销售反而有所增长。

paragraphs.en: “Health is kind of the new wealth in China,” said Rebecca Cai, Asia-Pacific general manager for Swiss premium running shoe brand On. The brand said in a May earnings call that quarterly sales in Greater China exceeded the Asia-Pacific regional growth figure of 44%.
paragraphs.cn: “在中国，健康可以说是一种新的财富，”瑞士高端跑鞋品牌“昂跑”（On）的亚太区总经理蔡以佳表示。该品牌在5月的财报电话会议上称，大中华区的季度销售额超过了亚太地区44%的整体增长率。

paragraphs.en: Some consumers trace the fitness trend to a postpandemic cultural shift. “After Covid, everything changed,” said Xu Lin, the owner of Prakasa, a popular yoga studio in Shanghai, “Everyone wants to have a better life, not just money, money, money, work, work, work.”
paragraphs.cn: 一些消费者将这一健身热潮归结于后疫情时期的文化转变。“新冠疫情之后，一切都变了，”上海一家热门瑜伽工作室“Prakasa”的老板徐琳（音译）说道，“每个人都希望过上更好的生活，而不只是‘钱、钱、钱，工作、工作、工作’。”

articles.source: 2026.8.15-身心健康E02 如何科学控糖？

paragraphs.en: In the case of sugar consumption, the two parallel pathways involve one pathway related to the actual taste and the perception of sweet tastes that lead not just you, but every animal that we're aware of to seek more sweet-containing foods. The other parallel pathway is related to the nutritive component of sweet foods, meaning the degree to which a given food will raise blood glucose.

But if you understand the way that dopamine works, what you'll realize is that when this dopamine pathway is triggered, it tends to create not the sensation or the perception of satiety of feeling like something is enough, but rather to produce the sensation of wanting more. In fact, we can say that the longer it's been since you've indulged in something that you really enjoy or would like, the greater the dopamine you will experience when you finally engage in that behavior or indulge that thing, ingest that thing.

So if you really wanted to adjust your sugar cravings and you really still want to ingest some sugary foods, you probably would be better off combining fiber with that sugary or sweet food. So what we're really talking about here is trying to reduce the dopamine signal that is the consequence of ingesting sweet foods.

There are now data pointing to the fact that lemon juice and lime juice, a couple of tablespoons or so, if ingested before or even during, or even after consumption of sugary foods, or I should say foods that sharply increase blood glucose or large carbohydrate meals can actually blunt the blood glucose response.

When you ingest lemon juice or lime juice, the mechanism by which it blunts blood glucose is probably twofold. One is probably through the post-ingestive effects of glucose in the gut, meaning the way in which sugars are interacting with neurons and other components of your gut circuitry to impact things like gastric emptying time, to impact things like the firing of those neuropod cells and their signaling to the brain. But almost certainly it has something to do also with the perception of sour taste on the tongue.

Using berberine is a serious step. You should absolutely talk to your doctor about it. It is true that if you ingest berberine, your blood glucose will plummet. And I point that out because I've actually tried it before. It gave me brutal headaches and I felt really dizzy and I felt like I couldn't see straight. And actually I couldn't see straight. Why did it do that? Well, it made me hypoglycemic. It actually drove my blood glucose down too far.

items.understanding: 糖的摄入。常搭配 caffeine consumption（咖啡因摄入）/ alcohol consumption（酒精摄入）。consumption 表"摄入量"。
血糖。日常也说 blood sugar，两者同义；blood glucose 更偏科学用语。延伸：glucose 葡萄糖 / fructose 果糖 / sucrose 蔗糖。
n. 通路、路径。神经科学常说 neural pathway（神经通路）；parallel pathways 两条并排跑、互不干扰的线路。
不是 A，而是 B。强调转折、突出后者（文中：not the sensation of satiety, but rather the sensation of wanting more）。
n. 饱足感、满足感（偏学术）。与 craving（渴望）相对。
v. 放纵、沉溺。indulge in something 放纵自己去享受某样东西（带点"明知不该还是忍不住"）。indulge in chocolate / a bad habit。
n. 强烈渴望。健康类高频：sugar craving 馋糖 / food cravings 馋食物 / carb cravings 想吃碳水。crave v. 强烈渴望（I'm craving chocolate. 我特别馋巧克力）。
v. 摄入。科普里说到把东西吃进身体基本用 ingest / consume，很少用 eat / drink。ingest sugary foods 摄入含糖食物。

items.text: you would be better off doing something
items.understanding: 你最好这么做、这么对你更有利。地道建议句式：You'd be better off sleeping early. 你最好早点睡 / You'd be better off talking to a doctor. 你最好去问问医生。
v.（本文）把劲头压下去、把锋芒磨掉。blunt the blood glucose response 把血糖反应的尖峰压平。adj. 钝的（a blunt knife 一把钝刀）。
n. 尖峰、峰值。blood glucose spike 血糖尖峰；可与 E01 的 cortisol spike（皮质醇峰值）对照。

articles.source: 2026.8.17-人形机器人第一股宇树上市，谁在疯狂押注？

paragraphs.en: Unitree’s IPO May Be Just the Beginning of an Investor Frenzy Over Humanoid-Robot Stocks
paragraphs.cn: 宇树科技的首次公开募股（IPO）可能只是投资者对人形机器人股票狂热追捧的开始

paragraphs.en: Unitree Robotics is set to become the first public humanoid-robotics company in mainland China, and it’s riding the robotics hype straight to the bank. Last week, the Hangzhou-based company priced its shares at about $22, seeking to raise about $900 million in an initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. On Monday, it said the IPO was more than 8,000 times oversubscribed by retail investors, a sign that interest in the burgeoning industry is strong.
paragraphs.cn: 宇树机器人即将成为中国大陆首家上市的人形机器人公司，并正借助机器人领域的市场热潮大举融资。上周，这家总部位于杭州的公司将股票定价定在22美元左右，计划在于上海证券交易所首次进行的公开募股（IPO）中筹集约9亿美元。周一，该公司表示，此次IPO获得了散户投资者超过8000倍的超额认购，这表明市场对这一蓬勃发展的新兴行业兴趣浓厚。

paragraphs.en: The market for humanoid robots is still pretty small — just 15,000 or so units were deployed last year — but advocates like Tesla CEO Elon Musk say the potential is massive. For now, Unitree sits near the top of the food chain.
paragraphs.cn: 人形机器人的市场规模目前仍然很小——去年仅部署了约1.5万台——但特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克等支持者认为，其市场潜力巨大。就目前而言，宇树科技处于该行业食物链的顶端。

paragraphs.en: Unitree was the single biggest supplier of humanoid robots last year, although it was outsold in the first half of 2026 by Chinese rival Agibot, according to a report from Smart Analytics Global. The top five suppliers were all Chinese firms. That’s largely because of how cheap Chinese robots are compared with rival products.
paragraphs.cn: 根据Smart Analytics Global的一份报告，宇树科技是去年人形机器人的最大单一供应商，尽管在2026年上半年，其销量被中国竞争对手智元机器人（Agibot）超越。前五大供应商均为中国企业。这很大程度上是因为中国机器人相较于竞争对手价格更为低廉。

paragraphs.en: Unitree is profitable, a relatively uncommon feat in the world of humanoid-robotics companies. Overseas sales accounted for over 40% of Unitree’s revenue in 2025, although the company has warned that geopolitical tensions could hamper its expansion. Last month, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission banned new foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots.
paragraphs.cn: 宇树科技已实现盈利，这在人形机器人行业中是难得的成就。2025年，海外销售额占宇树科技营收的40%以上，不过该公司已发出预警，地缘政治的紧张局势可能会阻碍其扩大规模。上个月，美国联邦通信委员会（FCC, Federal Communications Commission）开始禁止新的国外制造的人形机器人和四足机器人。

paragraphs.en: Unitree is not the only such firm seeking to go public. “Listing is a must,” LimX Dynamics founder Will Zhang told reporters in July.
paragraphs.cn: 宇树科技并非唯一一家寻求上市的公司。今年7月，逐际动力（LimX Dynamics）创始人张巍（Will Zhang）对记者表示：“上市是必须的。”

paragraphs.en: Agility Robotics plans to become the first pure-play public humanoid-robotics company in the U.S. The firm’s Digit robots are operating in commercial environments with GXO Logistics. “We have not achieved \[return on investment\] on humanoids yet,” Patrick Kelleher, the CEO of GXO, told investors last week.
paragraphs.cn: Agility Robotics计划成为美国第一家纯做人形机器人业务的上市公司。该公司的Digit机器人已经在GXO Logistics的商业环境里投入运行。GXO首席执行官帕特里克·凯莱赫（Patrick Kelleher）上周对投资者表示：“我们尚未在人形机器人上实现投资回报。”

items.understanding: 狂热。原文说宇树 IPO 点燃了投资者对人形机器人股票的 frenzy。看市场情绪可用 a buying frenzy（抢购潮）。提醒自己：frenzy 往往伴着泡沫，别被 hype 带节奏。

items.text: riding the robotics hype straight to the bank
items.understanding: 蹭热度、一路赚大钱。宇树借着机器人 hype 大举融资。口语可用 laugh all the way to the bank（轻松发大财）。夸一家趁势而起的公司：it rode the AI hype to a record valuation。
items.hl: riding the robotics hype straight to the bank

items.understanding: 超额认购。宇树 IPO 获散户超 8000 倍 oversubscribed，需求火爆。相关：subscribe 订阅 / 认购；subscribe for shares 认购股份。看新股热度时常用。
新兴的、快速冒头的。the burgeoning industry 新兴产业，可替换 an emerging industry。写趋势文高频：a burgeoning market for X。
（本文）部署、投放。去年全球才 deploy 了约 1.5 万台人形机器人。广义也指调派人手 / 资金：The bank deployed 200 staff。看规模落地时用。
主张者、鼓吹者。马斯克等 advocates 看好机器人潜力。作动词 advocate (doing) 主张（做）。表达立场观点时可用。
卖得比……多。宇树上半年被对手 Agibot outsold。out- 前缀表“胜过”：outperform 表现更好、outnumber 数量更多。读行业报告常用。
需要本事才能做成的事。宇树已盈利，在这行是 uncommon feat。辨析：achievement 偏中性，feat 暗含“这可不容易”的赞叹。夸人可用 no small feat。
占比。2025 年海外销售 accounted for 超 40% 营收。句型：A accounted for X% of B。写数据论证时高频。
阻碍、拖累。地缘紧张可能 hamper 其扩张。近义 hinder / impede。写风险段常用：Poor roads hamper aid delivery。
上市。宇树不是唯一一家 seeking to go public 的公司。同义 list / list on an exchange。财经新闻高频。
（本文）挂牌上市。创始人说“Listing is a must”。拓展：listed in Hong Kong 在港上市；IPO 首次公开发行。比 go public 更书面。
单一业务的。Agility 想做美国首家 pure-play 人形机器人公司。投资语境：a pure-play bet on lithium 纯押注锂，而非什么都做的巨头。看赛道纯度时用。
投资回报（ROI）。GXO 坦言人形机器人尚未实现 ROI。缩写 ROI 高频。评估任何投入都绕不开：what’s the ROI?

articles.source: 2026.8.18-镜像时代：我们看自己越多，为什么反而越不自在？

paragraphs.en: All This Staring at Our Faces Is Messing With Our Heads
paragraphs.cn: 总盯着自己的面孔看，正在扰乱我们的心智

paragraphs.en: Everything is strange. We socialize online. Our private lives are increasingly public. People pretend to be brands; brands pretend to be people. We optimize our bodies until they break. And the more we know, the less secure we feel.
paragraphs.cn: 一切都变得怪异。我们在网上社交，私人生活却日益公开化。个人把自己包装成品牌，品牌却要打造自己的“人”感。我们不断优化自己的身体，直至把身体搞垮。我们知道得越来越多，内心反而越来越没有安全感。

paragraphs.en: To know the truth of ourselves, we begin at what feels like a natural place: the mirror. We are constantly confronted with our own image: on our phones, front-facing videos, public spaces, our social media profiles, Zoom calls. But we can forget that mirrors both duplicate reality and reverse it. None show you exactly as you are.
paragraphs.cn: 为了认清真实的自我，我们会从一个看似理所当然的地方着手：镜子。我们不断看见自己的影像：手机屏幕、前置摄像头录制的视频、公共场合、社交媒体个人主页、线上视频会议。但我们有时会忘记，镜子既复刻现实，也会颠倒现实。没有一面镜子能呈现你真实的模样。

paragraphs.en: The historian Christopher Lasch wrote that “for the narcissist, the world is a mirror.” Almost 50 years later, this remains a tidy diagnosis, but it doesn’t quite capture the extent of the spiritual crisis that we’re now facing.
paragraphs.cn: 历史学家克里斯托弗・拉斯奇（Christopher Lasch）曾写道：“对自恋者而言，整个世界就是一面镜子。” 近五十年过去，这依旧是一个精辟的论断，但它已然没法涵盖我们当下面临的这场精神危机的严重程度。

paragraphs.en: I believe the room of mirrors that constantly surrounds us conjures something unsettling, something dark. It is a spiritual trap in which the imagined displaces the real: We choose a fantasy of ourselves over the reality of others. And that trap is baited and facilitated by technology.
paragraphs.cn: 我认为时刻将我们包围的镜像空间，会催生出某种令人不安、阴郁的东西。这是一处精神陷阱：想象取代了现实，我们宁愿沉溺于自我幻想，也不愿接纳他人的真实。而科技为这个陷阱设置诱饵，并推波助澜。

paragraphs.en: As more and more of our lives take place in a virtual realm, and we increasingly identify with the fantasies of our digital doppelgängers, we begin to dehumanize ourselves, and when we do this, it is undoubtedly easier to dehumanize others.
paragraphs.cn: 随着我们越来越多地活在虚拟世界里，我们会愈发认同自己数字化“分身”所承载的幻想，我们开始剥离自身的人性；一旦如此，我们无疑也更容易去漠视他人的人性。

paragraphs.en: When we look solely at ourselves, we fail to encounter anything that resists us; there are no contradictions, no interruptions. We need the honest gaze: the gaze of others and the gaze toward others. To see ourselves clearly, we don’t use mirrors. We use relationships.
paragraphs.cn: 当我们只盯着自身，就遇不到任何与自己相悖的事物；没有矛盾，也没有来自外界的打断。我们需要真诚的注视：来自他人的注视，以及投向他人的注视。想要看清自我，依靠的不是镜子，而是人与人之间的关系。

paragraphs.en: Mirrors encourage us to choose the fantasies of ourselves over the realities of others. It’s best we look away.
paragraphs.cn: 镜子怂恿我们沉溺自我幻想，无视他人的真实。我们最好移开目光。

items.understanding: 凝视、长时间盯着看（带过度感）。原文标题 “All This Staring at Our Faces Is Messing With Our Heads”——总盯着自己的脸看，反而扰乱心智。手机前置摄像头让我们天天都在 stare at 自己，适度就好。
扰乱、干扰、把……搞乱。原文 “messing with our heads”（扰乱我们的心智）。也常说 Too much screen time can mess with your sleep（刷太多手机影响睡眠）。
优化、使尽可能好。原文 “We optimize our bodies until they break”——不断优化身体直至搞垮。提醒自己：optimize 也要有度，别为优化把自己累垮。
面临、遭遇（带躲不开的强迫感）。原文 “We are constantly confronted with our own image”——不断面对自己的影像。比 face 多一层“避无可避”的意味。
复制。原文 “mirrors both duplicate reality and reverse it”——镜子既复刻现实也颠倒现实。注意它还有“重复、雷同”的引申义。
反转、逆转。原文 “mirrors… reverse it”（颠倒现实）。常见 reverse the decline（扭转下滑）。
自恋者。原文引拉斯奇 “for the narcissist, the world is a mirror”（对自恋者，世界就是一面镜子）。词源是希腊神话美少年 Narcissus。
描绘、捕捉（强调准确呈现）。原文 “doesn’t quite capture the extent of the spiritual crisis”——没能完全捕捉这场精神危机的程度。Words can’t capture how I feel（言语无法表达我的感受）。
唤起、引发（像用魔法变出）。原文 “conjures something unsettling”——催生出某种令人不安的东西。The magician conjured up a dove（魔术师变出一只鸽子）。
取代、使离开原位。原文 “the imagined displaces the real”——想象取代了现实。Convenience displaces quality（便利取代了质量）。
使便利、促进。原文 “baited and facilitated by technology”——由科技设置诱饵并推波助澜。比 help 更正式，常用于“促进某事发生”。
认同、自我代入、产生共鸣。原文 “identify with the fantasies of our digital doppelgängers”——认同数字化分身的幻想。Children identify with characters on screen（孩子会代入银幕角色）。
（本文）电子分身、另一个自己。原文 “digital doppelgängers”。来自德语，指“长得一模一样的另一个自己”，传说中是不祥之兆。
把目光移开。原文结尾 “It’s best we look away”——我们最好移开目光。呼应主题：看清自己不能靠镜子，而要靠与他人的关系。

articles.source: 2026.8.19-身心健康E03 减脂，原来并没有那么难

paragraphs.en: Lose Fat with Science-based Tools

So a calorie is a calorie as a unit of energy, and we need to accept and acknowledge this calories in, meaning calories ingested versus calories burned formula, but the calories burned portion is strongly influenced by a number of things that you can control that can greatly accelerate or increase the amount of adipose tissue or the proportion of adipose tissue that you burn in response to exercise and food.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

paragraphs.en: To mobilize fat, you got to break the backbone between glycerol and these fatty acids, okay? That’s accomplished by an enzyme called lipase, but you can forget all that if you want. Remember, we’re just trying to mobilize fat. So the first step is to get those fatty acids moving around in the bloodstream, to get them out of those fat cells, and then they can travel and be used for energy.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

paragraphs.en: They’re going to go into cells that can use them for energy. And once they are inside those cells, they’re still not burned up. You need to oxidize them. They need to be moved into the mitochondria and then they can be converted into ATP into energy. So just to really zoom out again to make sure I don’t lose anybody, you got to mobilize the fat, then you have to oxidize the fat.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

paragraphs.en: What they did was they examined people who overate and did not gain weight. And what they observed was that those people engaged in lots of subtle movement throughout the day. In other words, they were fidgeters and that’s what they call them. And in 2015, and again in 2017, there’ve been studies that have explored this using some modern metabolic tracking. And indeed, simply moving a lot, being a fidgeter, bouncing your knee, standing up and pacing several times or many times throughout the day, led to considerable amounts of fat loss and weight loss when people were ingesting the same amount of food.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

paragraphs.en: Those subtle movements of our core musculature, not just the core, but all our limbs and our musculature, those low level movements, they trigger epinephrine release from these neurons and they stimulate the mobilization of fat. And then that fat is oxidized at higher rates. So what’s the protocol? Fidget.

If you’re really interested in burning calories and you already exercise, you want to burn more, or you don’t have the opportunity to exercise or you’re averse to exercise for whatever reason, fidgeting movements, staccato movements, standing up, walking around, pacing, all the sort of nervous activities that we’re so critical of in other people and sometimes in ourselves are actually mobilizing and oxidizing a lot of fat and a lot of energy. And while this probably won’t compensate for chronic overeating, the caloric burn from this is considerable, and very likely can offset a meal that had excessive calories or a kind of steady state of eating too much.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

paragraphs.en: Caffeine can enhance the amount of fat that you burn in any duration of exercise, and it can shift the percentage of fat that you oxidize compared to glycogen. Unless you take that caffeine and it ramps you up so much that you’re training really, really intensely. The bottom line is if you like caffeine and you can use it safely, ingesting somewhere between 100 and 400 milligrams of caffeine prior to exercise, somewhere between 30 to 40 minutes before exercise can be beneficial if we’re talking about fat oxidation, burning more body fat.
paragraphs.cn:
-   身心管理小结  
    第二个减脂小建议：运动前喝一些含有咖啡因的饮料，可能有助于燃脂，但切记谨慎操作。因为对于使用咖啡因减脂，还有两个关键的前提条件：一，you like caffeine，你的确喜欢咖啡因，喝了之后没有难受的感觉；二，you can use it safely，你能合理、安全地使用它。因为咖啡因摄入过量可能引起不适，且因人而异。

paragraphs.en: There is really solid evidence from the Gardner Lab at Stanford and from other labs showing that when you look at different types, you look at low fat diets, high fat diets, keto diets, intermittent fasting, provided people stick to their particular diet, it doesn’t really matter which diet you follow. You can still get a caloric deficit and you get weight loss. Adherence, however, is always an issue. And so what I always say is that you want to use the eating plan that is obviously beneficial to your health, but the one that allows you to adhere to whatever it is that the particular nutrition protocol is, right? If you can’t stick with something, then it’s not very worthwhile.
paragraphs.cn: · 表达：词汇和短语

items.understanding: n. 卡路里（能量单位）。减脂的本质是 calories burned > calories in（消耗 > 摄入）。
n. 脂肪组织。运动与饮食能影响你燃烧的 adipose tissue 比例。
v. 加速（强调速度）。文中与 increase 并列：accelerate / increase the amount of adipose tissue you burn。
v. 调动、使……动起来。减脂第一步是 mobilize fat（让脂肪从细胞里“动”出来）。
n. 脂肪酸。脂肪要先变成 fatty acids 进入血液才能被利用。
n. 酶。分解甘油与脂肪酸靠一种叫 lipase 的 enzyme（记不住细节也没关系）。
v. 氧化。脂肪“动”出来后还要 oxidize（氧化）才能真正燃掉。
n. 线粒体。脂肪被送进 mitochondria 才转化为 ATP / 能量。
（口语）拉远镜头 → 引申为“跳出细节看主线”。主播说 let's zoom out 就是在帮听众回顾全景。
n. 总爱动来动去的人（fidget v. 做小动作）。研究发现不胖的人多是 fidgeters，常动更燃脂。
n. 肌肉系统 / 肌肉群（区别于单块 muscle）。core musculature 的低强度活动能促脂肪动员。
adj. 不想做、抵触（比 don't like 更正式强烈）。Some people are averse to exercise. 有人特别不愿运动。
n. 间歇性断食。keto / low-fat / high-fat diets / intermittent fasting——只要能坚持，哪种都行。
v. 坚持（某事）。provided you stick to a diet, 具体哪种饮食法不重要，能 stick to 才关键。

articles.source: 2026.8.20-越来越多夫妻，把“全职带娃补偿”写进了“婚前协议”

paragraphs.en: The Trigger Clause More Couples Want in Their Prenups
paragraphs.cn: 越来越多情侣希望在婚前协议中加入的“触发条款”

paragraphs.en: From her perch in Midtown Manhattan, divorce attorney Lisa Zeiderman has seen every imaginable marital horror story. Near the top of the list: Divorces where the spouse who stays home with the children is left with very little after decades of marriage.
paragraphs.cn: 在位于曼哈顿中城的办公室里，离婚律师丽莎·扎伊德曼（Lisa Zeiderman）见识过各种各样你能想象到的婚姻恐怖故事。其中最恐怖的莫过于：当数十年的婚姻走到尽头，留在家中抚养孩子的一方最终落得几乎一无所有。

paragraphs.en: But over the last couple of years, she is increasingly being asked to craft prenuptial agreements that include a “leaving the workforce” trigger. It activates if one spouse decides to stay at home and give up a career.
paragraphs.cn: 但过去几年中，越来越多的人找她起草包含“退出职场”触发条款的婚前协议。如果婚姻中的一方决定照顾家庭并放弃事业，该条款就会生效。

paragraphs.en: Anna Morgenstern, 40 years old, and Zach Spiess, 45, used an online platform to create their own agreements. The trigger they agreed on ensured the working spouse—whoever it would be—would provide additional financial support if one of them left the workforce, except in the case of infidelity.
paragraphs.cn: 40岁的安娜·莫根施特恩（Anna Morgenstern）和45岁的扎克·斯皮斯（Zach Spiess）选择使用一个在线平台来创建自己的婚前协议。他们商定的触发条款约定，如果其中一方退出职场，继续工作的另一方——无论具体是谁——将为对方提供额外的财务支持，除非存在婚姻不忠行为。

paragraphs.en: “It was a good opportunity to get a view into how he thinks about our future,” Morgenstern said. The process became a kind of financial planning exercise.
paragraphs.cn: “这是一次很好的机会，让我了解他如何看待我们的未来，” 莫根施特恩说道。整个过程某种程度上变成了一次财务规划演习。

paragraphs.en: One way to structure the provision is to have the working spouse set aside money that would reflect the stay-at-home parent’s previous salary, as well as 3% to 5% annual raises. Or the working spouse could contribute regularly to an investment account that goes solely to the other parent in a divorce.
paragraphs.cn: 构建该条款的方式之一是让工作的配偶预留一笔资金，该资金应反映全职在家一方先前的薪水外加每年3%至5%的涨幅。或者，工作的配偶可以定期向一个投资账户存钱，一旦离婚，该账户的资金将完全归另一方所有。

items.understanding: 触发条款：合同中某个特定事件或条件一旦满足，相应的权利义务便自动生效。前缀 trigger 本义是“扳机/引发后续结果的事件”。
n. 婚前协议（prenuptial agreement 的简称）；prenuptial 意为“婚前的”，nuptial 意为“婚姻的”。
（本文）n. 居高临下的位置、有利的观察点；本义指鸟类栖息的高枝。文中 From her perch in Midtown Manhattan 形容律师身处曼哈顿中城、俯瞰全局的视角。

items.text: over the last couple of years
items.understanding: 在过去几年中。over 强调某段时间内持续、渐进的变化或积累，区别于 during 的静态贯穿。
items.hl: over the last couple of years

items.understanding: （本文）v. 精心起草、拟定；本义 n. 手工艺。近义词 draft（起草）。
全面而长期地退出劳动力市场（为照顾家庭而放弃事业）。
v.（条款/机制）生效、激活——使预先订立却处于休眠状态的安排，在特定条件满足后转入生效状态。
v. 确保……发生（to make sure that something happens）。
除……情况之外（unless it is a case of …）。
深入了解、得以窥见（get insight into）。
n. 条款（侧重条款所表达的实质内容）；区别于 clause——clause 指法律文件结构上的单元（如第 3.1 条）。
为特定目的留出（资金、时间等）；reserve or keep for a particular purpose。
v. 与他人一道支付（部分或全部）资金，以划入共同基金或用于共同目的。

articles.source: 2026.8.21-英语正在“通货膨胀”：Very贬值后，下一个是谁？

paragraphs.en: How We Speak Has Gotten Extravagant. Literally.
paragraphs.cn: 我们说话的方式，变得越来越浮夸了。简直了。

paragraphs.en: What was once a single exclamation point now has to be (at least) two. Instead of just saying, “It was insane,” someone will say, “It was actually insane,” or, to the dismay of many, “It was literally insane.”
paragraphs.cn: 曾经一个感叹号就足以表达情绪，如今至少要用上两个。人们不再只说“这太离谱了”，有的人会说“这真的太离谱了”，或者，更让人看不下去的是，还有人会说，“这简直太离谱啦”。

paragraphs.en: Why can’t we just tamp it down and relax? The reason is that human conversation is not only about making statements, but about making statements worth your interlocutor’s attention.
paragraphs.cn: 我们为什么不能收敛一点、放松一点？原因在于，人类的交谈不只是为了陈述，更是为了做出值得你对话者注意的陈述。

paragraphs.en: This means that language is always drawing new things into the churn to keep us sounding urgent, committed. The linguist Martin Haspelmath calls this “extravagance,” where we operate according to the maxim “Talk in such a way that you will be noticed.”
paragraphs.cn: 这意味着，语言总在把新东西卷进这台搅拌机，好让我们听起来热切、恳切。语言学家马丁· 哈斯佩尔马特把这种现象称为“浮夸”——我们的说话方式遵循着这样一条准则：“以会被注意到的方式说话。”

paragraphs.en: This extravagance is behind much of what can sound like jittery filler. “Yeah, no” is a great example. The “no” does not contradict the “yeah” but complements it. “Yeah, no” is a stronger version of “yeah.”
paragraphs.cn: 许多听起来像是紧张兮兮的口头禅，背后都是这种浮夸。“Yeah, no”（是，不）就是个绝佳的例子。这个“不”并不否定那个“是”，而是在为它加码。“Yeah, no”是“yeah”的加强版。

paragraphs.en: In this vein, English is always and forever seeking new ways of saying “truly” in an emphatic, collar-clutching manner. In the 1300s “very” was the one to beat, but over time it lost its semantic punch.
paragraphs.cn: 循着这条脉络，英语永远都在寻找新的方式，以一种激烈的、揪住人衣领般的姿态来说“真的”。14世纪，“very”是无人能敌的那一个，但随着时间流逝，它的语义力道也消磨殆尽。

paragraphs.en: Or, yes, “literally insane,” or “I was literally dying of thirst so we stopped at a 7-Eleven.” Because in this usage of “literally,” we do not actually mean that we were about to perish from clinical dehydration. But words often have contradictory meanings with no one batting an eye. A chair is stuck fast to the floor, but a rabbit runs fast. The figurative use of “literally” is never confusing. It’s just one more way of having a “truly” that pops.
paragraphs.cn: 或者，这么说没错（literally insane）“简直离谱”，又或者（I was literally dying of thirst）“我简直要渴死了，所以我们在一家711停了一下”，这么说也没错。因为在“literally”的这种用法里，我们并不真的在说：我们快要因为临床意义上的脱水而丧命了。而词语还常常自带相互矛盾的含义，却没有谁为此眨一下眼。椅子纹丝不动（fast）地钉在地上，兔子跑得飞快（fast）。“Literally”的比喻用法从来不会造成误解。它不过是又一个让“（truly）真的”这个词砰然作响的方式罢了。

paragraphs.en: Not long ago I heard someone praising my tween daughter’s new hair color as “tuff.” OK, that one is weird to me — but in the end, it’s a more extravagant way of saying “cool.” “Cool,” after all, is a tad elderly now to get the job done.
paragraphs.cn: 前不久，我听到有人夸我十来岁女儿的新发色“tuff”。好吧，这个用法对我来说是有点怪——但说到底，它不过是“cool”的一种更浮夸的说法。毕竟，“cool”如今上了年纪，已经有点干不动这份活了。

items.understanding: 浮夸的、过度铺张的。原文标题 “How We Speak Has Gotten Extravagant” ——我们的说话方式变浮夸了。形容超出必要的华丽或夸张，可说 The party was extravagant（排场太大）。提醒自己：表达到位就好，别为强调而 extravagant。
字面上；口语里常作夸张强调，约等于“简直”。原文 “It was literally insane” 并不是真疯，而是“简直离谱”。母语者现在满嘴 literally 加强语气，理解成“简直 / 说真的”即可，不必较真字面义。
疯狂的、离谱的（口语高频）。原文 “It was insane” = 这太离谱了。比 crazy 稍正式，年轻人爱用 That’s insane 表惊叹。注意它本义是“精神失常”，口语里已弱化为程度副词。
实际上；此处用于给语气“加码”——“It was actually insane” 比 “It was insane” 多一层强调。聊天里 actually 常被当加强语而非真正转折，别误读成“然而”。
沮丧、惊愕。原文 “to the dismay of many”（令许多人侧目 / 无语）。常用 to one’s dismay 表“让人失望的是”。写作可用：To my dismay, it rained.（糟糕，下雨了。）
收敛、压低（情绪或表达）。原文 “tamp it down and relax” ——收一收、放松点。tamp 本义“捣实、夯实”，tamp down 引申为把过头的表达“压下去”。想劝人别太用力表达时可用。
对话者、交谈对象（较正式）。原文 “worth your interlocutor’s attention” ——值得你对话方的注意。词根 locu- 与 locution（措辞）同源。口语可换 conversation partner，正式 / 写作场合用 interlocutor 更准。
（此处）搅拌、翻腾。原文 “drawing new things into the churn” 把语言比作搅拌机，不断搅进新词。本义指搅奶油（churn butter），引申“剧烈翻动”，如 churn out（大量炮制）。
紧急的、热切的。原文 “sounding urgent, committed” ——听起来急切又恳切。形容需优先处理的事用 urgent；也指语气上的“急迫感”，比 emergency 更偏感受层面。
浮夸、铺张（名词）。原文语言学家称这种现象为 “extravagance”。对应形容词 extravagant。形容语言或消费上的“过度加码”都可用，如 the extravagance of his language。
紧张不安的、神经质的。原文 “jittery filler” ——紧张兮兮的口头禅。形容人焦虑手抖可用 feel jittery；形容话语 / 行为不稳也可用。jitter 本义“抖动”。
填充物；（此处）口头禅、filler word。原文 “sound like jittery filler” ——听着像紧张填充语。“Yeah, no” 这类就是 filler。口语里 um / like 也算 filler，演讲想干净就少放。
强调的、有力的。原文 “in an emphatic, collar-clutching manner” ——以一种揪住衣领般用力强调的姿态。emphatic statement = 掷地有声的声明。比 strong 更突出“着重”。
语义的。原文 “lost its semantic punch” ——“very” 失去了语义上的力道。semantic 指“意义层面”，semantic difference = 意义上的差别。和 grammatical（语法）相对。

articles.source: 2026.8.22-AI 垃圾内容刷屏，谁能吃到这波红利？

paragraphs.en: Can You Get Rich Quick Off A.I. Slop?
paragraphs.cn: 你能靠 AI 垃圾内容快速致富吗？

paragraphs.en: If you’re aware of slop, you probably see it everywhere. If you aren’t, you probably still see it everywhere and just don’t know it.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你知道“垃圾内容”是什么，你大概随处都能看到它；如果你不知道，你可能同样随处都能看到它，只是没意识到罢了。

paragraphs.en: Ambiguous content, quick scenes, cutting off the final speaker — these techniques are as essential to A.I. slop as the iamb and rhyme scheme are to a sonnet.
paragraphs.cn: 内容含糊不清、场景切换飞快、最后一位说话的人还没讲完就被切断——这些技巧之于AI垃圾内容的重要性，就像抑扬格和押韵格式之于十四行诗一样。

paragraphs.en: Once, slop was just what was fed to pigs: scraps of unwanted food and refuse. To understand modern slop, you have to think of humans as consuming content in the same way that pigs consume food. The goal of pig slop is to maximize nutrient intake while minimizing cost; the goal of A.I. slop is to maximize time spent consuming content while minimizing cost.
paragraphs.cn: 曾经，slop只指喂猪的东西：没人要的剩饭剩菜和垃圾。要理解现代意义上的slop（垃圾内容），你得把人类消费内容的状态看成猪吃食物一样。猪食的目标是在最大限度提高营养摄入量的同时，将制作成本降至最低；而AI泔水的目标，则是在最大限度提高人们花在内容上的时间的同时，将制作成本降至最低。

paragraphs.en: As a creator, once you join the network, you can apply to work on specific campaigns (most of which are based on A.I. slop), and your application will be evaluated by a campaign manager. Posts are submitted to an oversight team. Although most creators make very little money in this way — Roman Khaves, the founder of Affiliate Network, told me that the top 10 percent of creators on his platform make 90 percent of the money.
paragraphs.cn: 作为创作者，一旦加入这个平台，你就可以申请参与特定的推广项目（其中大多数都建立在 AI 垃圾内容之上），你的申请会由项目经理评估。发布的内容还要提交给审核团队。不过，绝大多数创作者靠这种方式赚不到多少钱——联盟网络（Affiliate Network）创始人罗曼·凯夫斯（Roman Khaves）告诉我，在他的平台上，排名前 10% 的创作者赚走了 90% 的钱。

paragraphs.en: There are, of course, other criticisms that can be leveled at A.I. slop: its contribution to reduced attention spans, a lack of human connection, an increasingly fuzzy border between advertising and entertainment, the eternal return of Tung Tung Tung Sahur. But, when I brought these things up with Khaves and his team, I heard a kind of social critique echoed back to me. Slop, they said, is the art of democracy. Khaves kept mentioning that “a guy in his parents’ basement” could now influence a large part of the culture.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，人们对 AI 垃圾内容还有其他方面的批评：导致注意力持续时间缩短，人际连接减少，使广告与娱乐之间的界限日益模糊，以及总会回到“Tung Tung Tung Sahur”之流上。然而，当我和凯夫斯及其团队提出这些问题时，他们却向我反馈了某种社会批判式的论调。他们认为，垃圾内容是一种民主的艺术。凯夫斯反复提到，如今哪怕只是“一个住在父母家地下室里的家伙”也有机会影响相当大一部分的文化潮流。

items.understanding: 从……，靠……。标题 “Get Rich Quick Off A.I. Slop” 里的 off = “靠 / 从……获利”，类似 live off something（靠某物生存）。别只记“离开”，在金钱 / 来源语境里它常表“凭借、依靠”。
泔水、剩饭、猪食；本文指低质 AI 生成的“垃圾内容”。原文 “A.I. slop” 就是喂给用户的低成本内容。可联想 workslop：看起来完成了，却没什么原创思考的工作成果。
知道、觉察到。原文 “If you’re aware of slop, you probably see it everywhere.” ——一旦注意到垃圾内容，你会发现它无处不在。反义 be unaware of，常用搭配 be aware of / become aware of。
打断（说话）、切断。原文 “cutting off the final speaker” ——还没讲完就被切断。电话、对话里常用：Sorry, we got cut off. 别打断我：Don’t cut me off.
抑扬格（诗歌节奏单位：轻-重）。原文把 AI 垃圾内容的制作技巧比作十四行诗里的 iamb。读诗、文学评论会碰到，口语里几乎不用，但知道它比“韵律单位”更专业。
韵律 / 韵法。原文 “rhyme scheme are to a sonnet” ——就像押韵格式之于十四行诗。scheme 这里不是“阴谋”，而是“安排、格式”。写诗歌分析可用。
剩菜剩饭；废料。原文 “scraps of unwanted food and refuse” ——没人要的食物残渣。引申义：metal scrap 金属废料；a few scraps of information 零星信息。普通人只分到 scraps = 残羹剩饭。
废物、垃圾（本文义）；也读 /rɪˈfjuːz/ 表“拒绝”。原文和 scraps 并列：unwanted food and refuse。注意同一个词两种读音两种意思，读作 /ˈrefjuːs/ 时是名词“垃圾”。
大量地吃、消耗、吞噬。原文 “humans as consuming content” 把人类消费内容比作猪吃食。社交媒体 consume time without you noticing ——不知不觉吞噬时间。比 use / eat 更有“被吞掉”的画面感。
推广营销项目、专项活动。原文 “work on specific campaigns” ——参与特定推广项目。也可指政治竞选：presidential campaign；营销活动：sales campaign。
监督、监管。原文 “submitted to an oversight team” ——提交给审核团队监管。over-（在上面）+ sight（看）= 从上往下看 =  oversight。注意它也可以指“疏忽、漏看”，但本文是“监管”。
瞄准、对准；引申为“对……提出（批评/指控）”。原文 “criticisms that can be leveled at A.I. slop” ——可以对 AI 垃圾内容提出的批评。常见搭配 level accusations at / level criticism at。
（本文）导致、促成；也表贡献。原文 “its contribution to reduced attention spans” ——它对注意力缩短所起的作用。注意“做出贡献”是 make a contribution to，这里的 to 后面接名词或动名词。
注意力集中的时长。原文 “reduced attention spans” ——注意力持续时间缩短。span 指一段时间，concentration span 同理。短视频刷多了，attention span 就会变短。
